title: Absolute Galois presentation of the fundamental group of a normal integral scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a normal integral scheme: it is integral in the sense of [def-pc-integral-scheme] and every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field at its generic point $\eta$, and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ with its profinite Krull topology. Choose an algebraic closure $\widetilde\Omega$ containing $\Omega$; automorphisms of $\Omega$ extend uniquely over the purely inseparable extension $\widetilde\Omega/\Omega$. For each $x\in X$, choose a strict henselization $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and a compatible $K$-embedding of its fraction field $K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ into $\Omega$. These strict henselizations are domains and such embeddings exist. Set $J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_{K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)\subseteq G$. Then the homomorphism $q_X:G\to\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$ induced by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with geometric generic point $\bar\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega$ and fundamental group as in [def-galois-fibre-functor], is continuous and surjective, and $\ker(q_X)$ is the smallest closed normal subgroup of $G$ containing all $J_x$. This holds for any such choices of the embeddings.
